## Connecting research and understanding.

I lead research and evaluation work in community mental health, drawing on graduate training in quantitative psychology. My interests include measurement, applied analysis, effective services, and clear communication of what evidence can—and cannot—tell us.

I also mentor doctoral psychology interns and am developing accessible resources to help students learn statistical reasoning through meaningful examples and guided practice.

## Featured publication

::: {.editorial-spotlight}

<span class="section-kicker">Peer-reviewed research · 2025</span>

<div class="spotlight-title">Telemental health and remote work: An exploratory analysis of their dual impact on mental health professionals’ experiences during COVID-19 stay-at-home orders</div>

Lizano, Bergen, Smith, Pasquarella, and Lee examine how the rapid shift to remote work and services shaped mental health professionals’ experiences, with implications for workforce well-being and clinical care.

[Read the publication](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11414-024-09925-z) · [See all publications](research.qmd)

:::

## Teaching resources in development

The first collection will support **Elementary Statistics** through short explanations, worked examples, interactive demonstrations, and guided interpretation. The course roadmap is available now as a proposed instructional design; individual simulations are not yet published.

[View the Elementary Statistics pathway](courses/elementary-statistics/index.qmd) · [Read about my teaching approach](teaching.qmd#teaching-approach)
